scenario: 很多候选人 ML SD 面试挂掉，不是因为不会某个技术，而是 6 步框架没走完。
scenario_en: Many candidates fail ML SD interviews not because they lack a skill but because they never finish the six-step framework.
q: ML SD 面试最主要的失败模式是什么？
q_en: What is the primary failure mode in ML SD interviews?
why: 首要失败模式是覆盖不全，而这几乎总是时间管理问题、不是知识问题——某一步陷太深，后面几步没时间讲。修法是主动预算时间、覆盖优先。
why_en: The primary failure is incomplete coverage, which is almost always a time-management problem rather than a knowledge gap.
options: 对某个模型或算法的理论理解不够深，被追问细节就露馅
覆盖不全——某一步陷太深，后面几步没时间讲
英语口语不够流利，表达跟不上思路，被反复打断
画的架构图不够漂亮、白板排版乱，视觉呈现差
options_en: Not understanding some model or algorithm deeply enough, exposed when they push on details.
Incomplete coverage — sinking too deep into one step leaves no time for the rest.
Not fluent enough in spoken English, so you keep getting interrupted.
The diagram is not pretty and the whiteboard layout is messy.
optionExplanations: 理论深度问题存在但不是首要杀手；大多数挂掉的人其实懂，只是没讲完。
对；覆盖不全＝时间管理失手，某步超时挤掉后面步骤，是本课点名的头号失败模式。
口语能加分但不是主因，一个结构完整的设计即使口语一般也能过。
图的美观度无关评分核心，评的是覆盖和取舍，不是画工。
optionExplanations_en: Theory depth matters but is not the top killer; most who fail actually know the material — they just did not finish.
Correct — incomplete coverage is a time-management miss where one step's overrun crowds out later steps, the number-one failure named here.
Fluency helps but is not the main cause; a complete design passes even with average English.
Diagram aesthetics are not the scoring core; coverage and tradeoffs are judged, not draftsmanship.

scenario: 同一道 ML SD 题，Staff+ 和初级工程师在时间分配上表现出不同习惯。
scenario_en: On the same ML SD prompt, Staff+ and junior engineers show different habits in how they allocate time.
q: 在时间分配上，Staff+ 和初级工程师的关键区别是什么？
q_en: In time allocation, what is the key difference between Staff+ and junior engineers?
why: 怎么分配分钟本身就是一个设计决策和资历信号：Staff+ 跨所有关注点做预算、保证全覆盖；初级工程师钻进自己最强的组件出不来。管理时间＝管理覆盖。
why_en: How you allocate minutes is itself a design decision and seniority signal: Staff+ budget across all concerns while juniors tunnel into their strongest component.
tradeoff: 跨所有步骤预算(全覆盖) vs 钻最强组件(局部深、整体缺)
options: Staff+ 在最强组件上钻得比初级更深，用极致深度取胜
Staff+ 跨步骤做预算保覆盖，初级钻进最强组件出不来
Staff+ 语速更快，能在一半时间里塞进两倍的内容
两者没区别，时间分配只是个人习惯，和资历评级无关
options_en: Staff+ go even deeper on their strongest component than juniors, winning on extreme depth.
Staff+ budget across steps to protect coverage; juniors tunnel into one component.
Staff+ simply talk faster, cramming twice the content into half the time.
No difference; time allocation is personal habit, unrelated to the seniority rating.
optionExplanations: 钻最深恰恰是初级的坑；Staff+ 反而克制单点深度以换全局覆盖。
对；跨步骤预算 vs 单点钻深，正是资历信号——评委看你能否管理整场覆盖。
讲快不等于讲全，塞两倍内容常是堆细节而非合理覆盖，反而是负信号。
时间分配恰恰是被评的资历信号，说它无关是忽略了本课的核心论点。
optionExplanations_en: Going deepest is exactly the junior trap; Staff+ restrain single-point depth to buy global coverage.
Correct — budgeting across steps vs tunneling on one point is the seniority signal; evaluators watch whether you manage whole-session coverage.
Talking fast is not covering fully; cramming twice the content is usually piling detail, a negative signal.
Time allocation is precisely the assessed seniority signal; calling it unrelated ignores this lesson's core point.

scenario: MAANG 面试官评分时，要在「完整但每步中等深度」和「某一步超强、但整体不完整」之间做取舍判断。
scenario_en: MAANG interviewers scoring must weigh a complete design with medium depth against a partial one with extraordinary depth in one area.
q: MAANG 评分偏好「广度优先」——具体怎么理解？
q_en: MAANG scores 'breadth before depth' — how should you read that?
why: 一个覆盖全、每步深度合理的完整设计，胜过某一步极深但整体残缺的设计。所以时间要优先铺满 6 步，再在余量里加深，而不是在一步上无限深挖。
why_en: A complete design with reasonable depth beats a partial design with extraordinary depth in one area, so spend time covering all six steps before deepening any one.
options: 在一个组件上做到全场最深，其他步骤略过也没关系
完整覆盖 6 步、每步深度合理，胜过单点极深但残缺
广度优先就是每步只说一句话，越浅越省时间越好
先把最难的一步做到完美，剩下的步骤看时间再说
options_en: Go deepest of anyone on one component; skipping other steps is fine.
Full coverage at reasonable depth beats one extraordinary step in a partial design.
Breadth-first means one sentence per step — the shallower and faster the better.
Perfect the hardest step first, then handle the rest with whatever time is left.
optionExplanations: 单点最深但整体残缺正是广度优先要否定的——覆盖不全是失败模式。
对；广度优先＝先保证 6 步都到位、深度合理，再谈局部加深，完整性权重最高。
广度优先不是要浅——是要合理深度下的完整，一句话带过每步同样不合格。
先把一步做到完美就会吃掉预算、挤掉其他步，正是广度优先反对的做法。
optionExplanations_en: Deepest-on-one-point but incomplete is exactly what breadth-first rejects; incomplete coverage is the failure mode.
Correct — breadth-first means covering all six steps at reasonable depth first, then deepening locally; completeness weighs most.
Breadth-first is not shallow; it is completeness at reasonable depth, and one sentence per step also fails.
Perfecting one step first eats the budget and crowds out others — exactly what breadth-first opposes.

scenario: 45 分钟的 ML SD 面试要在 6 步之间分配时间，每步有默认预算。
scenario_en: A 45-min ML SD interview splits time across six steps, each with a default budget.
q: 填空：6 步框架的默认时间预算（分钟）。
q_en: Fill in: the default per-step time budget (minutes) of the framework.
text: 问题澄清 {{3-5}} 分钟，数据策略 {{5-7}}，模型设计 {{8-10}}，评估 {{5-7}}，部署 {{7-8}}，监控 {{5-7}}，留 {{3-5}} 分钟做 buffer/Q&A。这些是给定的节奏目标，不是公式推导。
text_en: Clarification {{3-5}} min, data strategy {{5-7}}, model design {{8-10}}, evaluation {{5-7}}, serving {{7-8}}, monitoring {{5-7}}, with {{3-5}} min buffer/Q&A. These are given pacing targets, not derived numbers.
why: 这套预算是给定的节奏目标（不是算出来的），模型设计占比最高（~20%）因为它信息量最大。它约束的是「每步别超预算、保证全覆盖」。
why_en: These budgets are given pacing targets, with model design highest at about 20%, and they constrain you to stay on pace and cover everything.

scenario: 你在模型设计上已经聊了 11 分钟还想继续深挖某个架构细节。
scenario_en: You have spent 11 minutes on model design and want to keep drilling into an architecture detail.
q: 关于单步时长，有条硬规则是什么？违反它的后果？
q_en: What is the hard rule on single-step duration, and the cost of breaking it?
why: 硬规则：任何单步都不要超过 10 分钟。超了就会挤掉后面步骤、导致覆盖不全——而覆盖不全是首要失败模式。10 分钟是最可靠的客观超时信号，到点就该收。
why_en: The hard rule is never more than 10 minutes on any single step, because overrunning crowds out later steps and causes incomplete coverage.
options: 没有硬规则，只要你觉得这步重要就可以一直讲下去
硬规则是每步至少讲满 10 分钟，讲太快会显得不深入
硬规则是任何单步不超过 10 分钟；超了会挤掉后面步骤、导致覆盖不全
硬规则是把 45 分钟平均分成 6 份，每份 7.5 分钟严格执行
options_en: There is no hard rule; if you feel a step matters you can keep going indefinitely.
The hard rule is at least 10 minutes per step; going faster looks shallow.
The hard rule is never more than 10 minutes on any single step; overrunning crowds out later steps and causes incomplete coverage.
The hard rule is to split 45 minutes evenly into six 7.5-minute slots, strictly enforced.
optionExplanations: 「觉得重要就一直讲」正是导致超时和覆盖不全的心态，本课明确设了 10 分钟上限。
方向反了：规则是上限不是下限，逼你别超时，不是逼你讲满。
对；10 分钟是单步上限，是最可靠的客观超时信号，到点就收以保覆盖。
预算不是平均分——各步默认时长不同，还要按题目重排，均分是误解。
optionExplanations_en: 'Keep going if it feels important' is exactly the mindset that overruns and undercuts coverage; the lesson sets a firm 10-minute cap.
Reversed: the rule is a ceiling not a floor, forcing you to stop, not to fill time.
Correct — 10 minutes is the per-step ceiling and the most reliable objective overrun signal; stop at the mark to protect coverage.
The budget is not split evenly; step defaults differ and get reordered per prompt, so even splitting is a misreading.

scenario: 每一步都有一个典型的「过度投入陷阱」，认得出来才能及时收手。
scenario_en: Each step has a typical over-investment trap; recognizing them lets you pull back in time.
q: 以下哪些是各步骤真实的「过度投入陷阱」？(多选)
q_en: Which of these are real over-investment traps for the steps? (multiple)
why: 真实陷阱：澄清阶段问太多澄清题却不收敛；数据阶段罗列每一个可能特征；模型阶段纠结层数/超参；评估阶段只列指标不挂业务。识别陷阱＝及时止损的前提。
why_en: Real traps: over-clarifying without converging, enumerating every feature, debating layer counts and hyperparameters, and listing metrics with no business tie-in.
options: 问题澄清：问一堆澄清题却迟迟不收敛
数据策略：把每一个可能的特征都枚举一遍
模型设计：纠结具体层数、超参数
监控迭代：一句话带过重训（这是投入不足，不是过度投入）
options_en: Problem clarification: asking many clarifying questions without converging.
Data strategy: enumerating every possible feature.
Model design: debating exact layer counts and hyperparameters.
Monitoring: a one-sentence mention of retraining (this is under-investment, not over-investment).
optionExplanations: 对；澄清题问不完却不收敛，是第 1 步的典型过度投入。
对；穷举特征是数据策略的过度投入，重点该是几个关键特征而非清单。
对；纠结层数/超参是模型设计的过度投入，应停在设计级取舍。
监控只讲一句是「投入不足」，恰恰相反——这题问的是过度投入。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — endless clarifying without converging is step 1's classic over-investment.
Correct — enumerating features is data-strategy over-investment; the focus should be a few key features, not a catalog.
Correct — debating layers and hyperparameters is model-design over-investment; stay at design-level tradeoffs.
A one-line monitoring mention is under-investment, the opposite of what this question asks about over-investment.

scenario: 你讲完了问题澄清，准备进入数据策略，想让面试官跟上并有机会重定向。
scenario_en: You finished clarification and are moving to data strategy, wanting the interviewer to follow and be able to redirect.
q: 为什么要用口头「转场信号」而不是默默切到下一步？
q_en: Why use a verbal transition signal instead of silently switching steps?
why: 口头转场＝转向灯，有三个作用：给面试官一个重定向的时机、展示结构化思维、制造检查点阻止沉默的时间漂移。默默切换会让面试官跟丢，也失去纠偏机会。
why_en: A verbal transition acts as a turn signal: it gives the interviewer a moment to redirect, demonstrates structured thinking, and creates checkpoints that stop silent time drift.
tradeoff: 口头转场(同步+给纠偏窗口) vs 默默切换(省几秒但面试官跟丢)
whenOtherWins: 若面试官已明确让你「继续下一部分」，简短一句衔接即可，不必每次都完整报「我做完了X，现在进入Y」。
options: 纯粹是礼貌用语，实质作用不大，省略掉也没关系
给面试官重定向时机、展示结构、设检查点防漂移
为了拖时间，给自己一个停顿几秒的正当借口
为了把每一步的结论重复两遍，加深面试官印象
options_en: Pure politeness; it has little real effect and can be skipped.
It gives the interviewer a moment to redirect, shows structure, and sets a checkpoint.
To stall for time and give yourself a legitimate excuse to pause a few seconds.
To repeat each step's conclusion twice so it sticks with the interviewer.
optionExplanations: 转场不只是礼貌，它有三个实打实的功能，省略会让面试官跟丢、错过纠偏窗口。
对；三个功能——重定向时机、展示结构、设检查点——正是转向灯的价值。
转场不是拖时间，它是主动同步和设检查点，把它当停顿借口是误解。
转场不是重复结论——它是一句简短过渡，重复反而浪费预算。
optionExplanations_en: A transition is not mere politeness; it has three concrete functions, and skipping loses the interviewer and the redirect window.
Correct — the three functions (redirect moment, show structure, set checkpoint) are exactly the turn-signal value.
A transition is not stalling; it actively syncs and sets checkpoints, so treating it as a pause excuse misreads it.
A transition is not repeating conclusions; it is one brief bridge, and repeating wastes budget.

scenario: 你把范围定到「Airbnb 搜索排序，200ms 延迟」，准备转入数据策略。
scenario_en: You scoped it to 'Airbnb search ranking under 200 ms' and are about to move into data strategy.
q: 填空：一句好的转场信号包含哪三块？
q_en: Fill in: what three pieces make a good transition line?
text: 「我已经把范围定到 {{Airbnb 搜索排序、200ms 延迟}}（回顾上一步结论），下面进入 {{数据策略}}（点名下一步）——{{sound good/可以吗}}？（征得同意）」
text_en: "I've scoped this to {{Airbnb search ranking under 200 ms}} (recap the prior step), moving to {{data strategy}} (name the next step) — {{sound good}}? (check in)"
why: 好转场＝回顾上一步结论＋点名下一步＋征得同意（sound good?）。这既设了检查点，又给面试官一个重定向的窗口。
why_en: A good transition recaps the prior step, names the next step, and checks in, setting a checkpoint and a redirect window.

scenario: 面试一开始你就在白板/共享文档顶部有块空间可以用。
scenario_en: At the interview's start you have blank space at the top of the whiteboard or shared doc.
q: 一个低成本的进度管理技巧是什么？
q_en: What is a low-cost progress-management trick?
why: 开场就把 6 步写在白板顶端，每完成一步就打勾——一个对双方都可见的进度条。它让你和面试官随时知道走到哪、还剩哪几步，天然防止时间漂移。
why_en: Write the six steps at the top of the whiteboard and check each off as you transition, a shared visual progress tracker that prevents time drift.
tradeoff: 白板进度条(占几秒但双方可见) vs 靠记忆(省时但易漂移)
whenOtherWins: 若是纯语音、没有共享白板的电话面，就用口头 recap 代替打勾，效果类似但要更勤地口头同步进度。
options: 把每一步的完整笔记都写满白板，越详细越好
开场把 6 步写在白板顶端，每完成一步就打勾
全程不写任何东西，靠记忆管理进度，显得从容
只在最后 5 分钟把走过的步骤补写上去，当作总结
options_en: Fill the whiteboard with complete notes for every step — the more detail the better.
Write the six steps at the top and tick each one off as you go.
Write nothing all session and manage progress from memory to look composed.
Only in the last 5 minutes, jot the steps you covered down as a summary.
optionExplanations: 写满详细笔记会占用宝贵时间还挡视线；进度条要的是简洁可扫读。
对；顶端列 6 步+打勾＝低成本进度条，双方随时看到走到哪、还剩几步。
纯靠记忆容易漂移，也让面试官看不到结构，反而不利。
最后补写起不到实时防漂移的作用，进度条的价值在过程中而非结尾。
optionExplanations_en: Filling in detailed notes eats precious time and blocks the view; a tracker should be terse and scannable.
Correct — six steps at the top plus checkmarks is a low-cost tracker so both sides always see position and remaining steps.
Memory-only invites drift and hides your structure from the interviewer, which hurts.
Writing it at the end gives no real-time drift protection; the tracker's value is during, not after.

scenario: 你需要在陷太深之前就察觉「我在这步待太久了」。
scenario_en: You need to notice 'I've been on this step too long' before you sink too deep.
q: 检测「过度投入某一步」有哪三个信号？
q_en: What are the three signals for detecting over-investment in a step?
why: 三个信号：10 分钟阈值（最可靠的客观信号）、细节层级漂移（开始争超参/层数而非设计级取舍）、面试官重定向提示（「我们继续吧」或问别的步骤）。任一出现就该收手。
why_en: Three signals: the 10-minute threshold (most reliable, objective), detail-level drift (debating hyperparameters instead of design tradeoffs), and interviewer redirect cues.
diagram:
flowchart TD
  A["在某步待太久?"] --> B["信号1: 超过10分钟(最可靠客观)"]
  A --> C["信号2: 细节漂移(争超参/层数)"]
  A --> D["信号3: 面试官重定向提示"]
  B --> E["进入恢复协议"]
  C --> E
  D --> E
options: 10 分钟阈值、细节层级漂移、面试官重定向提示
自己感觉累了、面试官打了个哈欠、白板写满了
已经讲了 3 个要点、喝了一口水、看了一眼时钟
面试官记笔记、你停顿了一次、麦克风有回声
options_en: The 10-minute threshold, detail-level drift, and interviewer redirect cues.
Feeling tired, the interviewer yawning, and the whiteboard being full.
Having covered 3 points, taking a sip of water, and glancing at the clock.
The interviewer taking notes, you pausing once, and mic echo.
optionExplanations: 对；10 分钟阈值（客观）＋细节漂移＋面试官重定向，是本课给的三个可操作信号。
累了/哈欠/白板满都是主观或无关线索，不构成可靠的超时判据。
讲了几点、喝水、看表都不是过度投入的判据，和时长信号无关。
记笔记、停顿、回声是噪声，不能用来判断你是否在某步陷太深。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — the 10-minute threshold (objective) plus detail drift plus interviewer redirect are the three actionable signals given here.
Tiredness, yawns, and a full whiteboard are subjective or irrelevant and are not reliable overrun criteria.
Covering points, sipping water, and clock-glancing are not over-investment criteria and are unrelated to duration signals.
Note-taking, a pause, and echo are noise and cannot indicate whether you have sunk too deep into a step.

scenario: 模型设计时你发现自己开始和面试官争「用 4 个还是 8 个注意力头」。
scenario_en: In model design you catch yourself debating '4 or 8 attention heads' with the interviewer.
q: 「细节层级漂移」这个超时信号具体长什么样？
q_en: What does the 'detail-level drift' overrun signal actually look like?
why: 细节漂移＝从设计级取舍掉进具体超参/层数/代码（如「4 还是 8 个注意力头」）。这类争论对整体设计几乎无增量，是你在这步陷太深的信号，该拉回设计级。
why_en: Detail drift is dropping from design-level tradeoffs into specific hyperparameters, layer counts, or code, like arguing 4 vs 8 attention heads.
tradeoff: 设计级取舍(该停留处) vs 超参/层数细节(漂移信号)
options: 从超参细节升回到设计级取舍——这是好现象，不是漂移
从设计级取舍掉进具体超参/层数/代码细节
从模型设计切换到评估步骤——正常转场，不算漂移
面试官突然问了一个和当前步骤无关的问题
options_en: Rising from hyperparameter detail back up to design-level tradeoffs — a good sign, not drift.
Dropping from design-level tradeoffs down into hyperparameters, layers, or code.
Switching from model design to evaluation — a normal transition, not drift.
The interviewer suddenly asking something unrelated to the current step.
optionExplanations: 方向反了：升回设计级是好事；漂移是往细节下沉，不是往上升。
对；掉进超参/层数这种低层细节，正是「陷太深」的典型表现，该拉回设计级。
切到下一步是正常转场，不是细节漂移，两个概念不同。
面试官问别的步骤属于「重定向提示」，是另一个信号，不是细节漂移。
optionExplanations_en: Reversed: rising to design level is good; drift is sinking into detail, not rising.
Correct — dropping into low-level detail like hyperparameters and layers is the classic 'too deep' symptom; pull back to design level.
Moving to the next step is a normal transition, not detail drift — different concepts.
The interviewer asking about another step is a 'redirect cue', a different signal, not detail drift.

scenario: 欺诈题上，你在特征工程已经花了 12 分钟，意识到超时了。
scenario_en: On a fraud prompt you have spent 12 minutes on feature engineering and realize you have overrun.
q: 把「过度投入后的 3 步恢复协议」排成正确顺序：
q_en: Order the 3-part recovery protocol after over-investment:
steps: 简短承认花了不少时间（不反复道歉）
当场给出这一步的决定（如：三个关键信号是交易速度、商户风险、设备指纹相似度）
立刻转入下一步（Moving to model design now）
why: 恢复协议＝承认→做决定→立刻走。关键是承认要简短、决定要果断、转场要立刻，别反复道歉。优雅的自我纠偏本身就是 Staff+ 信号。
why_en: The recovery protocol is acknowledge, decide, move on immediately, keeping the acknowledgment brief and the transition instant.
diagram:
flowchart LR A["1 简短承认
花了些时间"] --> B["2 当场给决定
top-3 信号"] B --> C["3 立刻转下一步
模型设计"]

scenario: 你意识到某步超时，很想连着说好几句「抱歉，我花太久了，真不好意思……」
scenario_en: Realizing you overran a step, you feel the urge to say several apologies in a row.
q: 超时后反复道歉会怎样？正确做法是什么？
q_en: What happens if you over-apologize after overrunning, and what is the right move?
why: 反复道歉浪费时间、还显得不够沉稳。正确做法是一句简短「我在这上面花得够多了」，然后果断给决定、立刻转场。压力下的优雅自我纠偏本身就是 Staff+ 评估信号。
why_en: Repeated apologies waste time and read as less composed, so give one brief acknowledgment then decide and transition, since graceful self-correction is itself a Staff+ signal.
options: 反复道歉显得谦逊有礼，面试官会因此给你加分
一句简短承认后果断转场，别反复道歉
干脆完全不承认超时，假装什么都没发生继续讲
先花一分钟解释为什么会超时，把原因说清楚再继续
options_en: Repeated apologies look humble and polite, so the interviewer gives you points.
One brief acknowledgment, then a decisive transition — no repeated apologies.
Just never acknowledge the overrun and carry on as if nothing happened.
Spend a minute explaining why you overran, make the cause clear, then continue.
optionExplanations: 反复道歉不是谦逊，它消耗预算又暴露慌乱，是减分不是加分。
对；一句简短承认＋果断转场既止损又显沉稳，优雅纠偏是 Staff+ 信号。
完全不承认会让面试官觉得你没意识到时间问题，缺乏自我监控。
花一分钟解释原因又是新的浪费，承认要简短，别把道歉换成长篇解释。
optionExplanations_en: Repeated apologies are not humility; they burn budget and signal fluster — a minus, not a plus.
Correct — one brief acknowledgment plus a decisive transition stops the loss and reads as composed; graceful self-correction is a Staff+ signal.
Never acknowledging makes the interviewer think you missed the time issue, showing weak self-monitoring.
A minute of explanation is fresh waste; keep the acknowledgment brief rather than swapping apology for a long explanation.

scenario: 题目是广告点击预测，1M QPS、sub-50ms。默认预算里模型设计 8-10 分钟、部署 7-8 分钟。
scenario_en: The prompt is ad-click prediction at 1M QPS, sub-50ms; default budget gives model design 8-10 min and serving 7-8 min.
q: 这种延迟关键的题，时间预算该怎么调？
q_en: For this latency-critical prompt, how should you reshuffle the budget?
why: 延迟关键题让 serving 主导：把部署提到 10-12 分钟、把模型设计压到 6-7 分钟。因为吞吐/延迟在你讨论前就淘汰了整类架构，serving 决策才是这题的重心。并显式说明这次重分配。
why_en: Latency-critical prompts let serving dominate, so give serving 10-12 minutes and compress model design to 6-7, because throughput eliminates architectures before you discuss them.
tradeoff: serving 深度(延迟先淘汰整类架构) vs 模型设计深度(取舍多但非瓶颈)
whenOtherWins: 若这题延迟宽松、瓶颈在建模质量，就保持默认预算，不必把部署拉长——重分配要由约束驱动。
options: 保持默认预算不变，延迟题也按标准 8-10 分钟讲模型
部署提到 10-12 分钟、模型设计压到 6-7 分钟
把评估拉到 12 分钟，因为延迟关键题最难定义指标
把监控拉长，延迟题上线后最容易出问题所以监控最重要
options_en: Keep the default budget unchanged; even a latency prompt gets the standard 8-10 min on models.
Give serving 10-12 min and compress model design to 6-7.
Stretch evaluation to 12 min because latency prompts are hardest to measure.
Stretch monitoring because latency prompts break most after launch, so monitoring matters most.
optionExplanations: 延迟题保持默认就浪费了主动重分配的判断力——约束已明显把重心推向 serving。
对；serving 主导＝把部署拉到 10-12、模型压到 6-7，因为延迟先砍掉一批架构。
延迟题难点在 serving 不在评估，把评估拉到 12 分钟是重心放错。
监控重要但不是这题的主导约束，延迟才是；拉长监控偏离了约束驱动的重分配。
optionExplanations_en: Keeping the default on a latency prompt wastes the judgment of a deliberate reshuffle; the constraint clearly shifts weight to serving.
Correct — serving dominates, so give it 10-12 and compress models to 6-7, since latency cuts architectures first.
The hard part of a latency prompt is serving, not evaluation, so stretching evaluation to 12 min misplaces the focus.
Monitoring matters but is not this prompt's dominant constraint — latency is; stretching monitoring departs from constraint-driven reshuffle.

scenario: 题目是生成式 AI（RAG、摘要），没有单一 ground truth，「好」很难定义。
scenario_en: The prompt is generative AI (RAG, summarization) with no single ground truth and 'good' hard to define.
q: 生成式 AI 题的时间预算该往哪倾斜？
q_en: Where should the time budget tilt for a generative-AI prompt?
why: GenAI 评估最难（无单一 ground truth），把评估拉到 8-10 分钟讲 LLM-as-judge、人工评估、忠实度；同时把部署压 -2 分钟（批/近实时常够用）。评估是这类题的重心。
why_en: For generative AI, evaluation is hardest with no single ground truth, so give evaluation 8-10 minutes for LLM-as-judge, human evaluation, and faithfulness, compressing serving by about 2 minutes.
tradeoff: 评估深度(无 ground truth，最难判好坏) vs 部署深度(批/近实时常够用)
whenOtherWins: 若这道 GenAI 题延迟极敏感（如实时对话助手），那 serving 又会回到重心，不能一味压部署。
options: 把模型设计拉到 12 分钟，专门讨论选哪个基座大模型
把评估拉到 8-10 分钟，部署相应压 -2 分钟
把数据策略拉到 10 分钟，因为 GenAI 成败全靠语料
保持默认预算，GenAI 和普通题的时间分配没区别
options_en: Stretch model design to 12 min just to discuss which base model to use.
Give evaluation 8-10 min and compress serving by about 2 min.
Stretch data strategy to 10 min because generative AI lives or dies on its corpus.
Keep the default budget; generative AI and ordinary prompts allocate time the same.
optionExplanations: GenAI 难点不在选哪个大模型，而在怎么评「好」，把模型拉到 12 分钟放错重心。
对；评估无 ground truth 最难，拉到 8-10 分钟讲 judge/人工/忠实度，压部署换出时间。
GenAI 也吃数据但这题的独特难点是评估，拉长数据没抓住主要矛盾。
GenAI 恰恰要往评估倾斜，说和普通题没区别就丢了域适配这个判断信号。
optionExplanations_en: The hard part of generative AI is not which large model but how to judge 'good', so stretching models to 12 min misplaces focus.
Correct — evaluation with no ground truth is hardest, so give it 8-10 min for judge/human/faithfulness and compress serving to fund it.
Generative AI uses data too, but this prompt's unique difficulty is evaluation, so stretching data misses the main tension.
Generative AI should tilt toward evaluation; saying it is no different forfeits the domain-adaptation judgment signal.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用一个大模型给另一个模型的输出打分/评判，替代部分人工评估。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: LLM-as-judge uses one large model to score another model's outputs, partly replacing human evaluation.

termDefinitions.meaning: 生成内容是否忠于检索到的证据、不编造，是 RAG 的关键评估维度。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Faithfulness is whether generated content stays true to the retrieved evidence without fabricating, a key RAG eval dimension.

scenario: 题目是欺诈或医学影像：标签质量差、类别极不平衡、数据是主要瓶颈。
scenario_en: The prompt is fraud or medical imaging: poor label quality, severe class imbalance, data is the bottleneck.
q: 数据稀缺/噪声标签的题，时间预算怎么调？
q_en: For a data-scarce, noisy-label prompt, how do you adjust the budget?
why: 数据是瓶颈时把数据策略拉到 8-10 分钟，深入讲标签质量、类别不平衡、新鲜度；相应把监控压 -2 分钟。数据决策决定了这类题成败。
why_en: When data is the bottleneck, give data strategy 8-10 minutes for label quality, class imbalance, and freshness, compressing monitoring by about 2 minutes.
tradeoff: 数据策略深度(标签/不平衡是瓶颈) vs 监控深度(可压 -2 分钟)
whenOtherWins: 若数据充足、瓶颈其实在延迟或评估，就别硬拉数据策略——重分配始终跟着真实瓶颈走。
options: 把模型设计拉到 12 分钟，用更复杂的模型硬扛数据不足
数据策略拉到 8-10 分钟，监控相应压 -2 分钟
把部署拉到 10 分钟，先想怎么上线再回头补数据
保持默认预算，数据问题在评估阶段一起处理就行
options_en: Stretch model design to 12 min and brute-force data scarcity with a more complex model.
Give data strategy 8-10 min and compress monitoring by about 2 min.
Stretch serving to 10 min; deploy first and circle back to data later.
Keep the default; handle data issues together in the evaluation step.
optionExplanations: 数据不足时上更复杂模型只会过拟合，问题在数据层，堆模型解决不了。
对；瓶颈在数据就把预算投到数据策略，深挖标签/不平衡/新鲜度，压监控换时间。
先想上线再补数据是把顺序和重心都放错，数据没解决上线也白搭。
数据问题不能拖到评估才处理，它从训练一开始就污染一切，要在数据策略解决。
optionExplanations_en: A more complex model on scarce data just overfits; the problem is at the data layer and cannot be piled-model away.
Correct — when data is the bottleneck, invest the budget in data strategy on labels, imbalance, and freshness, compressing monitoring to fund it.
Deploy-first-then-data misplaces both order and focus; unsolved data makes launch pointless.
Data issues cannot wait for evaluation; they pollute everything from training onward and must be solved in data strategy.

termDefinitions.meaning: 正负样本比例极端悬殊（如欺诈只占 0.1%），会让模型偏向多数类。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Class imbalance is an extreme skew between positive and negative samples (e.g. fraud is 0.1%), biasing the model to the majority class.

scenario: 你正按计划推进，面试官接连追问「怎么扛流量尖峰？」「feature store 挂了怎么办？」
scenario_en: You are on plan when the interviewer repeatedly asks 'handle a traffic spike?' and 'what if the feature store is down?'
q: 面试官反复追问 serving，你该怎么调整时间？
q_en: The interviewer keeps probing serving — how do you adjust time?
why: 面试官反复问某一步＝在告诉你他想看这里的深度，就顺势在 serving 上多花时间、讲深。反过来「行了，我们继续吧」就是让你立刻压缩转场。跟着面试官的线索走。
why_en: Repeated serving questions signal the interviewer wants depth there, so go deeper on serving, while 'that's fine, let's move on' means compress and transition immediately.
tradeoff: 跟着面试官线索加深 serving vs 守住原定预算保后续覆盖
whenOtherWins: 若面试官只是顺口一问、并未反复深挖，就简短回答后按原计划继续，不必大改预算。
options: 无视追问，坚持自己的时间计划把 serving 快速带过
顺势在 serving 上多花时间、讲得更深
把追问都推到最后 Q&A 环节统一回答，先走完流程
反问面试官为什么老问 serving，先搞清他的意图
options_en: Ignore the probes and stick to your plan, breezing past serving quickly.
Go deeper on serving right there, following the interviewer's lead.
Defer all probes to the final Q&A and finish the flow first.
Ask the interviewer why they keep asking about serving to clarify intent first.
optionExplanations: 无视反复追问会错过面试官明确给的信号，坚持原计划反而显得不会读场。
对；反复追问是重定向信号，顺势深挖 serving 正是跟着面试官线索的域适配。
把追问推到最后会让面试官觉得你回避，实时的深挖才是他想要的。
反问动机会显得防御，面试官的意图已经很清楚——他想看 serving 深度。
optionExplanations_en: Ignoring repeated probes misses the interviewer's explicit signal, and sticking to plan reads as failing to read the room.
Correct — repeated probing is a redirect signal, so deepening serving follows the interviewer's cue — domain adaptation in action.
Deferring probes to the end makes the interviewer feel dodged; real-time depth is what they want.
Questioning their motive reads as defensive; the intent is already clear — they want serving depth.

scenario: 你还想在评估上多说两句，面试官说了句「That's fine, let's move on」。
scenario_en: You want to add more on evaluation, but the interviewer says 'that's fine, let's move on.'
q: 听到「行了，我们继续吧」这类提示，正确反应是什么？
q_en: On hearing 'that's fine, let's move on', what is the right response?
why: 这是明确的重定向提示：立刻压缩当前步、马上转场，别再补充。硬要多说会显得没读懂信号、也在浪费双方时间。面试官的节奏优先于你的计划。
why_en: It is a clear redirect cue, so compress the current step and transition immediately rather than adding more.
whenOtherWins: 若你判断当前这点是整题成败的关键、漏了会答不完整，可以用一句话说明「我补一句关键取舍就转」，但要极简。
options: 坚持把想说的评估细节补完，专业性不能打折
立刻压缩当前步、马上转场，别再补充
反问面试官「您是觉得这块不重要吗」再决定
假装没听见，继续按自己原本的节奏讲完
options_en: Insist on finishing the evaluation details you planned; professionalism must not be compromised.
Compress the current step and transition right away, adding nothing more.
Ask back 'do you think this part is unimportant?' before deciding.
Pretend not to hear and keep going at your own original pace.
optionExplanations: 硬补细节是没读懂信号，专业性不体现在无视提示上，反而显得不会配合。
对；「let's move on」是重定向提示，立刻压缩转场才是读懂了场、尊重面试官节奏。
反问会显得防御和纠缠，面试官已经明确表态，无需追问动机。
假装没听见是最差反应，直接踩了「无视重定向」的雷。
optionExplanations_en: Forcing details ignores the signal; professionalism is not shown by ignoring a cue, and it reads as uncooperative.
Correct — 'let's move on' is a redirect cue, so compress and transition immediately, which shows you read the room and respect their pace.
Asking back reads as defensive and clingy; the interviewer has been explicit, so probing motive is needless.
Pretending not to hear is the worst response, stepping straight on the 'ignore the redirect' landmine.

scenario: Airbnb 排序题进行到第 18 分钟，你正深挖 re-ranking，面试官突然问「position bias（位置偏差）怎么处理」——它其实是数据/标签层面的问题。
scenario_en: At minute 18 on an Airbnb ranking prompt, deep in re-ranking, the interviewer asks about position bias — really a data/label-level concern.
q: 18 分钟深挖 re-ranking 时被问 position bias，最好的处理是什么？
q_en: At 18 min deep in re-ranking, asked about position bias — best move?
why: 简短承认它是与评估相关的数据/标签问题，简洁作答，并在 2 分钟内信号转场到评估。既回应了面试官，又不在 re-ranking 上继续超投、把话题拉回时间线。
why_en: Briefly acknowledge it as a data/label concern tied to evaluation, answer concisely, and signal a transition to evaluation within two minutes.
tradeoff: 就地深挖 position bias(答得透) vs 简洁作答 2 分钟内转场(保后续覆盖)
whenOtherWins: 若才刚进入这一步、时间还很充裕，可以就地把 position bias 讲得更展开些，不必急着 2 分钟内转场。
options: 停下 re-ranking，花 8 分钟专门深挖 position bias 的各种去偏方法
简短承认它是与评估相关的数据/标签问题，简洁作答，2 分钟内信号转场到评估
回一句「这个不重要」，继续讲 re-ranking
承认自己不懂 position bias，直接跳过这个问题
options_en: Stop re-ranking and spend 8 minutes deep-diving every position-bias debiasing method.
Briefly acknowledge it as a data/label concern tied to evaluation, answer concisely, and signal a transition to evaluation within 2 minutes.
Say 'that's not important' and keep talking about re-ranking.
Admit you do not know position bias and just skip the question.
optionExplanations: 已经 18 分钟还花 8 分钟深挖 position bias 会严重超时，挤掉后面步骤。
对；简短承认+简洁作答+2 分钟内转场，既回应又止损，把话题顺势带回评估。
把面试官的问题说成不重要既失礼又错判——position bias 确实影响标签质量。
直接说不懂并跳过丢掉了展示判断的机会，其实你能把它归到评估/标签去回应。
optionExplanations_en: At 18 minutes, an 8-minute deep dive on position bias badly overruns and crowds out later steps.
Correct — brief acknowledgment, concise answer, transition within 2 minutes both responds and stops the loss, steering back to evaluation.
Calling the interviewer's question unimportant is rude and wrong — position bias really does affect label quality.
Just admitting ignorance and skipping forfeits a chance to show judgment; you can tie it to evaluation/labels instead.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用户更爱点靠前的结果，导致点击标签高估了排在前面的项，是数据/标签层的偏差。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Position bias is that users click higher-ranked results more, so click labels overstate top items — a data/label-level bias.

termDefinitions.meaning: 排序后再对 top 结果做二次调整（如多样性、去重、业务规则）。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Re-ranking adjusts the top results after initial ranking, e.g. for diversity, dedup, or business rules.

scenario: 6 步默认预算里，模型设计拿到的时间占比最高。
scenario_en: In the default budget, model design gets the highest share of time.
q: 模型设计的默认预算约 8-10 分钟（~20%）意味着什么？
q_en: What does model design's default 8-10 min (~20%) budget imply?
why: 8-10 分钟是给定的节奏目标（不是算出来的），~20% 占比最高，因为模型设计信息密度大、取舍最多。但它仍受 10 分钟硬上限约束，超了就要压缩转场。
why_en: The 8-10 minutes is a given pacing target and the highest share at about 20% because model design is the most information-dense step, still capped at 10 minutes.
options: 意味着模型设计可以随便超时、突破 10 分钟硬上限，因为它是六步中最重要的一步
占比最高(~20%)的给定节奏目标，但仍受 10 分钟硬上限约束
意味着其他 5 步必须各压缩到 3 分钟以内，把时间都让给模型设计
意味着这个数字是从 45 分钟总时长精确算出的最优值，换题也不会变
options_en: It means model design can freely overrun past the 10-minute hard cap, because it is the most important of the six steps.
It is a given pacing target with the largest ~20% share, still under the 10-minute cap.
It means the other five steps must each compress under 3 minutes to hand time over to model design.
It means the number is a precisely computed optimum from the 45-minute total, fixed across prompts.
optionExplanations: 占比最高不等于可以超时——10 分钟硬上限对每步都适用，模型设计也不例外。
对；8-10 分钟是给定目标、~20% 最高份额，但硬上限仍是 10 分钟，超了就压缩。
其他步不必压到 3 分钟以内，各有自己的默认预算，这是过度牺牲。
它是给定的节奏目标不是算出来的最优值，且会按题目域重分配。
optionExplanations_en: The highest share does not permit overrunning; the 10-minute cap applies to every step, model design included.
Correct — the 8-10 min is a given target and the highest ~20% share, but the hard cap stays at 10 minutes, so overrun means compress.
Other steps need not compress under 3 minutes; each has its own default budget, so this over-sacrifices.
It is a given pacing target, not a computed optimum, and it gets reallocated by prompt domain.

scenario: 你对模型架构最擅长，忍不住在模型设计上讲了 15 分钟，越讲越细。
scenario_en: Strongest at model architecture, you cannot resist spending 15 minutes on model design, getting finer and finer.
q: 钻进自己最强的组件出不来，会付出什么代价？
q_en: What is the cost of tunneling into your strongest component?
why: 在最强组件上超投＝后面的评估、部署、监控没时间讲，导致覆盖不全（首要失败模式）。而且这暴露了初级信号——不会跨关注点做预算。深度救不了缺失的广度。
why_en: Over-investing in your strongest component leaves no time for evaluation, serving, and monitoring, causing incomplete coverage and exposing a junior signal.
options: 没什么代价，把最强的一块讲透就能盖过其他步的缺失
后面几步没时间讲，导致覆盖不全，还暴露初级信号
只会让面试官觉得你谦虚，因为你没有炫耀其他技能
面试官会因为你在一处的深度而自动补满其他步的分
options_en: No cost; nailing your strongest part outweighs missing the other steps.
Later steps get no time, causing incomplete coverage and exposing a junior signal.
It just makes the interviewer think you are modest for not showing off other skills.
The interviewer auto-fills the other steps' scores because of your depth in one place.
optionExplanations: 单点深度盖不过整体缺失——广度优先下，覆盖不全就是失败，深度补不回。
对；钻深＝挤掉后面步骤＝覆盖不全，同时暴露不会做全局预算的初级信号。
超投一处不是谦虚，恰恰是失控的表现，和谦虚无关。
面试官不会替你补分——没讲到的步骤就是没有信号，深度不能转移。
optionExplanations_en: Single-point depth cannot outweigh overall gaps; under breadth-first, incomplete coverage is failure and depth cannot recover it.
Correct — tunneling crowds out later steps into incomplete coverage while exposing a junior signal of no global budgeting.
Over-investing in one place is not modesty; it is loss of control, unrelated to modesty.
The interviewer does not fill in scores for you; unspoken steps yield no signal and depth does not transfer.

scenario: 超时后你要用一个固定的 3 步套路把自己拉回正轨。
scenario_en: After overrunning you use a fixed 3-part routine to get back on track.
q: 填空：过度投入后的 3 步恢复协议。
q_en: Fill in: the 3-part recovery protocol after over-investment.
text: 恢复协议＝{{承认花的时间}}（简短、不反复道歉）→ {{给出决定}}（如 top-3 信号）→ {{立刻转场}}到下一步。
text_en: Recovery protocol = {{acknowledge time spent}} (briefly, no over-apologizing) → {{state the decision}} (e.g. top-3 signals) → {{move on}} immediately to the next step.
why: 承认→决定→转场，三步都要快。核心是承认简短、决定果断、转场立刻，让优雅的自我纠偏本身成为 Staff+ 信号，而不是慌乱的道歉循环。
why_en: Acknowledge, decide, move on, all quickly, so that graceful self-correction becomes a Staff+ signal rather than a fluster of apologies.

scenario: 时间不够时，很多人干脆把「部署上线」整步跳过不讲。
scenario_en: Short on time, many people just skip the entire serving/deployment step.
q: 把部署这步整个跳过，会造成什么后果？
q_en: What is the consequence of skipping the serving step entirely?
why: 整步跳过部署＝丢掉一整块系统思维信号（延迟、吞吐、扩展、feature store），这是覆盖不全最严重的一种。宁可每步压薄、也要 6 步都触及；系统思维正是部署这步在评的。
why_en: Skipping serving forfeits an entire block of systems-thinking signal (latency, throughput, scaling, feature store), the worst form of incomplete coverage.
options: 没关系，部署是运维的事，ML 面试不看这块
丢掉一整块系统思维信号，是最严重的覆盖不全
反而加分，说明你懂得取舍、敢于砍掉次要步骤
只影响 Staff+ 评级，对 Senior 及以下没有影响
options_en: It is fine; serving is ops work and ML interviews do not assess it.
It forfeits a whole block of systems-thinking signal — the worst incomplete coverage.
It actually adds points, showing you can prioritize and dare to cut minor steps.
It only affects Staff+ ratings and has no impact at Senior or below.
optionExplanations: 部署恰恰是 ML SD 在评的系统思维，不是纯运维，跳过就丢了这块分。
对；整步跳过＝丢一整块系统思维信号，比每步压薄严重得多，覆盖不全就是失败模式。
砍掉整步不是取舍是遗漏——取舍是压薄不是跳过，跳过整步是负信号。
系统思维在各级别都被评，跳过部署对 Senior 同样扣分，不只 Staff+。
optionExplanations_en: Serving is exactly the systems thinking ML SD assesses, not pure ops, so skipping forfeits that score.
Correct — skipping the whole step drops an entire systems-thinking block, far worse than thinning each step; incomplete coverage is the failure mode.
Cutting a whole step is omission, not prioritization; prioritizing means thinning, not skipping, and skipping is a negative signal.
Systems thinking is assessed at every level, so skipping serving penalizes Senior too, not just Staff+.

scenario: 面试官不只看你设计得对不对，也在看你怎么分配这 45 分钟。
scenario_en: The interviewer watches not only whether your design is right but how you allocate the 45 minutes.
q: 为什么说「怎么分配时间」本身就是被评估的内容？
q_en: Why is 'how you allocate time' itself something being assessed?
why: 时间分配本身是一个设计决策和资历信号：它反映你能否在有限预算下管理覆盖、识别重心、按约束重排。管不好时间＝管不好一个真实项目的范围。
why_en: Time allocation is itself a design decision and seniority signal, reflecting whether you can manage coverage and reprioritize under a fixed budget.
options: 因为面试官需要凑够评分项，时间只是用来凑数的
时间分配本身就是设计决策，反映你能否管理覆盖与重心
因为面试有硬性 KPI 要求必须用满 45 分钟
因为讲得越久越显得内容多，时间长短直接等于分数高低
options_en: Because the interviewer needs to pad the rubric, so time is just filler.
Time allocation is itself a design decision, showing whether you manage coverage.
Because interviews have a hard KPI to use the full 45 minutes.
Because talking longer looks like more content, so duration equals score.
optionExplanations: 时间不是凑数项，它直接映射到「能否管理一个真实项目范围」的判断。
对；分配时间＝管理覆盖与重心的能力，这正是资历信号，和管真实项目同构。
没有「用满 45 分钟」的 KPI，重点是合理覆盖而非填满时间。
讲得久≠内容多，冗长反而是负信号，时长不等于分数。
optionExplanations_en: Time is not filler; it maps directly to the judgment of whether you can manage a real project's scope.
Correct — allocating time is the ability to manage coverage and focus, exactly the seniority signal, isomorphic to running a real project.
There is no 'fill 45 minutes' KPI; the point is reasonable coverage, not maxing time.
Talking longer is not more content; verbosity is a negative signal, and duration does not equal score.

scenario: 面试压力下你意识到跑偏了，能不能干净利落地把自己拉回正轨，本身也在被观察。
scenario_en: Under pressure you realize you drifted, and how cleanly you pull yourself back is itself being observed.
q: 在压力下优雅地自我纠偏，对评分意味着什么？
q_en: What does gracefully self-correcting under pressure mean for scoring?
why: 压力下的优雅自我纠偏本身就是 Staff+ 评估信号——它证明你有自我监控、能果断止损、不慌乱。所以恢复协议不只是补救，执行得干净利落反而是加分点。
why_en: Graceful self-correction under pressure is itself a Staff+ signal, proving self-monitoring and decisive recovery without panic.
options: 是中性的，纠不纠偏、纠得好不好都不影响面试官对你资历的评分
优雅纠偏本身就是 Staff+ 信号，证明你有自我监控
是负信号，一旦纠偏就暴露你之前跑偏了，不如硬撑到底装作没事
只对时间管理这一项打分有用，和整体资历评级完全无关
options_en: It is neutral; whether and how well you self-correct does not affect the interviewer's seniority scoring.
Graceful self-correction is itself a Staff+ signal, proving you monitor yourself.
It is a negative signal — correcting exposes that you drifted, so better to push through and act like nothing happened.
It only helps the time-management score and is entirely unrelated to overall seniority rating.
optionExplanations: 纠偏质量不是中性——干净利落的自我纠正是被明确评估的能力。
对；优雅纠偏证明自我监控和沉稳，是本课点名的 Staff+ 加分信号。
纠偏不是暴露弱点，硬撑跑偏才是；果断止损远好于将错就错。
它直接关联资历评级（Staff+ 信号），不只是时间分。
optionExplanations_en: Correction quality is not neutral; clean self-correction is an explicitly assessed ability.
Correct — graceful correction proves self-monitoring and composure, a Staff+ plus this lesson names.
Correcting is not exposing weakness; pushing through the drift is; decisive recovery beats compounding the error.
It ties directly to seniority rating (a Staff+ signal), not just the time score.

scenario: 问题澄清阶段，你已经问了七八个澄清问题，还在继续追问更多细节。
scenario_en: In clarification you have already asked seven or eight questions and keep probing for more detail.
q: 问题澄清阶段的过度投入陷阱是什么，怎么避免？
q_en: What is the over-investment trap in clarification, and how do you avoid it?
why: 陷阱是问一堆澄清题却不收敛。避免法：3-5 分钟内锁定目标、规模、延迟这几个关键约束就收敛出一句精确问题陈述，然后转场。澄清是为了收敛，不是无限提问。
why_en: The trap is asking many clarifying questions without converging, so within 3-5 minutes lock the key constraints into a precise problem statement and move on.
tradeoff: 多问澄清题(信息更全) vs 3-5 分钟内收敛(保住后面 5 步预算)
whenOtherWins: 若题目极度模糊、关键约束确实还没交代清楚，可以多问一两个，但仍要在 5 分钟内收敛出问题陈述。
options: 陷阱是问得太少，应该尽可能多问、覆盖所有可能情况
陷阱是问而不收敛；3-5 分钟内锁定关键约束就转场
陷阱是不该问任何澄清题，直接开始设计最省时间
陷阱是把澄清题写在白板上，占用了后面画图的空间
options_en: The trap is asking too few; ask as many as possible to cover every possibility.
The trap is asking without converging; lock the key constraints within 3-5 min, then move on.
The trap is asking any clarifying questions at all; just start designing to save the most time.
The trap is writing clarifying questions on the whiteboard, using up later drawing space.
optionExplanations: 问得越多越好正是陷阱本身——不收敛的提问会吃掉预算、拖慢全局。
对；澄清的目的是收敛，3-5 分钟锁定目标/规模/延迟就出问题陈述，然后转场。
完全不问会漏掉关键约束、方向可能全错，走另一个极端也不对。
占用白板空间不是这里的陷阱，真正的陷阱是问而不收敛。
optionExplanations_en: More is better is the trap itself; non-converging questions eat the budget and slow everything.
Correct — clarification aims to converge; lock objective/scale/latency in 3-5 min into a problem statement, then transition.
Asking nothing misses key constraints and may go entirely wrong — the opposite extreme is also wrong.
Using whiteboard space is not the trap here; the real trap is asking without converging.
